issues.detail: Mostly happy-path code with little error handling, such as missing objects or a missing action, an empty channelbag, or find() returning None outside one case. The Guidelines and a few inline notes cover only some pitfalls.

scenarios.name: walk-cycle-nla-wave-layer
scenarios.rationale: Both layer a COMBINE wave strip starting at frame 25 on a second NLA track, set rotation_mode to XYZ, clear animation_data.action, name the actions, and run with blender --background --python; A also switches to Pose mode before keying, as the rubric asks, while B keys in Object mode.

scenarios.name: fix-fcurves-attribute-error-loop-noise
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses the channelbag helper, iterates channelbag.fcurves, adds the Cycles modifier, and finds the Z curve with fcurves.find("location", index=2) before adding Noise with strength and scale. A gets the channelbag helper and the modifiers right but finds the Z curve by looping over data_path and array_index instead of fcurves.find. A also claims 4.4+ keeps a legacy action.fcurves shim, which is questionable, and its explanation of slots and channelbags is thinner than B's.

scenarios.name: smile-shape-key-and-driver
scenarios.rationale: Both create Basis with from_mix=False, keyframe Smile at 0/1/0 using keyframe_insert, and set up a SCRIPTED driver with a LOC_X transform variable on the empty and an expression using the variable name; B is slightly cleaner (explicit animation clearing, fuller driver explanation), while A adds a vertex deformation but its keyframes-vs-driver conflict handling is only a note.
